instructions: Say this like an excited, energetic TikTok science creator: fast, punchy, amazed, with dramatic emphasis.
lines: It rains diamonds on Neptune. Real diamonds. And no, this is not a joke!
Neptune is the farthest planet from the Sun. Four and a half billion kilometers away.
Up there, it's minus two hundred degrees, and the winds hit over two thousand kilometers per hour. The fastest in the whole solar system!
But the craziest part is hidden deep inside. Under the clouds, there's a hot, dense ocean of water, ammonia and methane.
Go thousands of kilometers down, and the pressure gets so insane, it literally rips methane apart.
And the carbon that's left? Scientists think it gets squeezed together... into diamonds!
Then they fall. Diamonds, sinking through the planet like rain. Over thousands of years, they might pile up into a whole layer of diamond around the core.
Sounds fake? In twenty seventeen, scientists actually did it on Earth. They blasted plastic with super powerful lasers, and for a split second... tiny diamonds appeared!
And on Neptune, some of these diamonds could weigh millions of carats.
Here's the wild part: planets like Neptune might be the most common type in our galaxy. So right now, it could be raining diamonds all over the universe.
Next time: what happens if you fall into a black hole? Follow, so you don't miss it!
